text: Teaching LLM inference from first principles by building a small engine in C++ and CUDA. Teaching LLM inference from first principles by building a small engine in C++ and CUDA. The series follows what happens between a prompt and a generated token, from loading model weights to running each part of the transformer on the GPU. Read Inference from Scratch (PDF) for 80+ pages of my handwritten notes and diagrams. I developed all of the writing in this PDF myself, with NO AI writing . Companion notes for every video are in the study-notes index , with separate Markdown and PDF folders. You can also read the complete PDF collection . Part 8 explains Prefill, Decode, and the KV Cache . Part 9 follows with Static and Continuous Batching , including the current paged cache and online-softmax decode attention. The Llama 3.2 1B inference path includes dense causal prefill, paged decode attention, and static or continuous batching. Model dimensions and the 2,048-token context remain fixed for this learning engine. The KV pool defaults to 128 MiB and can be set with --kv-cache-mib N ; active request capacity follows the workload's page budgets rather than a fixed two-request limit. Admission guarantees room for each request's maximum processed prefix: prompt_tokens + allowed_new_tokens - 1 , rounded up to 16-token pages in each of the 16 layers. The allowed output budget is clamped to the context limit, and the final predicted token is returned without being processed again. These admission credits are separate from physical pages, which are assigned lazily. Early completion releases both the assigned pages and the remaining credits. Requests wait in FIFO order when their budgets cannot fit alongside active requests. Active requests have room to finish, so future page-boundary growth cannot exhaust the pool or deadlock generation. A request whose budget exceeds the entire pool is rejected with a clear error. This conservative policy avoids preemption and recomputation; a large requested output budget can limit concurrency even if the model eventually stops early. --stats reports the pool size, peak active requests, largest decode batch, peak assigned pages, admission waits, and final free-page count. Prefill still processes one prompt at a time between decode iterations. BF16 computations can round differently at different batch sizes. When vocabulary logits are nearly tied, greedy output tokens can therefore differ between individual and batched runs. Bitwise output equality across batch sizes is not guaranteed. mkdir -p models/llama-3.2-1b-instruct cp models/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct/original/tokenizer.model models/llama-3.2-1b-instruct/ cmake -S . -B build cmake --build build -j ./build/samir-vllm " Explain the KV cache in two sentences. " 128 # Continuous batching (default): admit requests whose page budgets fit. ./build/samir-vllm " Say hello. " 64 " Explain the KV cache. " " What is RoPE? " # Static batching: wait for the current group before admitting more. ./build/samir-vllm --static " Say hello. " 64 " Explain the KV cache. " " What is RoPE? " # More than two requests share the same default 128 MiB pool. ./build/samir-vllm --stats " Explain paging. " 64 " Explain GQA. " " Explain RoPE. " " Explain softmax. " # A smaller pool queues requests when their declared budgets cannot fit together. ./build/samir-vllm --kv-cache-mib 8 --stats " Explain paging. " 64 " Explain GQA. " " Explain RoPE. " ./build/tokenizer-test models/llama-3.2-1b-instruct/tokenizer.model After optional --static , --continuous , --kv-cache-mib N , and --stats flags, the first argument is a prompt and the second is max_new_tokens (default: 128). Any remaining arguments are additional prompts; the token budget applies to each request. Every prompt is formatted as an Instruct user message. Generation stops independently at EOS, EOT, or EOM, or the output/context limit, and each completed response is printed with its token IDs and request number. Prompts are prefilled one at a time, pausing decode. Each decode step packs one token from every active sequence into the shared buffers. Attention reads only that sequence's cache; requests can have different prompt and output lengths. Continuous batching admits waiting requests when page credits become available, while static batching admits the next group after the current group finishes. src/ Engine entry point, CUDA kernels, and tokenizer implementation include/ Public kernel and tokenizer headers tests/ Tokenizer tests python/ Tokenizer reference script proper_notes/ Study-notes index, markdown/ sources, and pdf/ reading editions scripts/ Rebuild the study-note PDFs notes.md Working notes from the build License The engine source code in src/ , include/ , tests/ , and python/ , along with CMakeLists.txt , .gitignore , and this README, is licensed under the MIT License .
